explanation: Robusta has nearly twice the caffeine of arabica, which is thought to help the plant fend off insects. It tastes more bitter and often goes into instant coffee and espresso blends.

claims.text: Arabica coffee beans typically contain about 1.2 to 1.5% caffeine by dry weight.
Robusta coffee beans typically contain about 2.2 to 2.7% caffeine by dry weight.
Caffeine is thought to help protect coffee plants from insects.
Robusta coffee tastes more bitter than arabica and is widely used in instant coffee and espresso blends.

A Wikipedia article on liberica coffee lists 1.61 g/100 g for arabica and 2.26 g/100 g for robusta, which is about 1.6% and 2.3%.
